items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Freddie Green was the wise old sage and also like a sergeant at arms

ctx.x: Do you remember -- I’ll come back to that. Just two questions. Describe for us or characterize for us how Basie exerted his leadership, and identify persons who had particular roles as lieutenants or whatever for him, and how one got status, or achieved tenure, or knew that one had achieved that.

We’ll start with Basie himself. One finger was all he needed to lead that band. He raised this finger and he might -- when he brought that finger down, music came from everywhere. As far as being a disciplinarian, he was very easy. He didn’t crack the whip. He wasn’t an a-h to get along with. He was wonderfully easy going. We could practically get away with murder as long as we came on time, dressed neatly, played 100 percent, and conducted ourselves as gentlemen on the bandstand. He didn’t have to put up with…

come on time, so why don’t you just go apologize to the chief?” We all called Basie “the Chief.” Nobody in the band called him -- referred to him as “Count.” It was “Chief” or “Bas.” Only outsiders called him “Count.” So I began a system of apologizing to the Chief. One time he said, “Man, you’re always sorry.” I think after that my habits cleaned up a little bit in the area of punctuality.

items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: And then the Freddie Green metronomic but still loose, happy rhythm

ctx.x: Yes they did. You’re making me cry for it.

And then the Freddie Green metronomic but still loose, happy rhythm, and Eddie Jones, who acquired a technique of walking the bass that was just phenomenal. And then Sonny Payne with the power that he gave to it. The All American Rhythm Section of the late 50’s. And hey—
It was a great time to be alive.

items.title: 68097_Freddie Green oral history interview
items.q: Well, you know, we got kind of back as a family thing after we -- you know -- after we got Frank Foster and Frank Wess.

ctx.x: And, yet as you watch a performance -- no matter who's up there in those or whatever it is -- guys are enjoying themselves -- year after year -- and decade after decade.
Well, you know, we got kind of back as a family thing after we -- you know -- after we got Frank Foster and Frank Wess.
